name: J02 — input, Unicode, resize and scrolling against the real product
about: J02 against the REAL PRODUCT — input, paste, Unicode, resize and scrolling.
PURPOSE, and why this exists alongside `j02-input.json`. That scenario runs
against the in-process contract double, which is the right place to drive
the terminal edge deterministically — but it cannot close a claim about the
product, and two of its steps are double conventions: it presses Enter on
The prefix is spelled for a SINGLE client because this runs through the
journey runner, which takes step values directly rather than per client; it
still selects the same model by filter and verifies the selection line.
the first model, and it waits for `echo <text>`, which is how the double
replies. Neither holds against a real provider.
So the navigation prefix here is the one the other journeys use, selecting
the SAME model by filter and verifying the selection line.
UNICODE IS ASSERTED TWICE, and the second time is the one that matters.
First in the COMPOSER, which tests the platform input path — a paste read
as bytes and rendered back. Then AFTER SUBMIT, where the text returns as
the durable user row: composed, sent, stored, re-listed and projected. A
composer-only assertion would prove the keyboard worked and nothing about
the wire.
THREE SCRIPTS, chosen for what each breaks. Latin-1 supplement (naïve,
café) catches a single-byte decode; an em dash and mathematical symbols
catch a cp1252 round trip; East Asian characters occupy TWO CELLS each and
catch a client that counts characters where it should count columns.
RESIZE HAPPENS WITH THAT CONTENT ON SCREEN, and the text is re-asserted
after each one. Capturing a frame after a resize proves the client did not
crash; requiring the wide characters to still be there proves it re-wrapped
them rather than truncating mid-character.
The multiline paste carries a REAL TAB and is deliberately not submitted at
that point — a newline inside a paste must not become an Enter that submits
half of it.
LIMITATION. This drives a real provider, so the assistant's reply is model
behaviour and nothing here asserts its content. Every assertion is about
text this scenario supplied and the product returned.
WHAT THIS SCENARIO DOES NOT COVER, so its receipt is not read for more than
it shows:
SCROLLING IS NOT ASSERTED HERE and its keystrokes are removed rather than
left in as decoration. This transcript is a few rows long, so PageUp has
nothing to travel through, and pressing a key without checking the view MOVED
is the exact defect corrected in j04-large-history. Scrolling movement,
including reaching the oldest line and returning to the tail, is proven
there.
LARGE PASTE is not covered: this pastes a short prompt. The bounded-paste
refusal path is exercised against the double, where a bound can be reached
deterministically.
FOCUS and INTERRUPTION are not covered here either. Focus is exercised in the
double run; interruption on the real product is j04-comparative, which drives
a live execution and requires the correlated terminal.

line one
	line two indented by a real tab
line three
